# Dual spaces

::: {#exr-dual-def} 
> Consider the function $F : C^\infty \to \mathbb R$ given by
> $$
> F(f) := f(2) - 3 f(1).
> $$
> 
> Recall that both $C^\infty$ and $\mathbb R$ are vector spaces.
> 
> Is $F \in ( C^\infty )^*$?
> If yes, verify that it is.
> If no, check that one of the conditions for $F$ to be in $( C^\infty )^*$ does not hold.
:::

::: {#exr-dual-in-coords} 
> Let $v,w \in \mathbb R^2$ and suppose we are in coordinates where
> 
> $$
> v = \begin{bmatrix}  1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} , \quad 
> w = \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}.
> $$
> 
> Let $F : \mathbb R^2 \to \mathbb R$ be a linear function given by
> 
> $$
> F(v) = 1 , \quad F(w) = 2.
> $$
> 
> Note that $F \in (\mathbb R^2)^*$.
> Find the matrix for $F$.
:::
